Pearson Whimsical Bird Sugarlift Aquatint Etching on Paper 12" x 8.2" Signed lower right This 1971 original intaglio print depicts an expressive, stylized long-legged bird reminiscent of an ostrich or emu, rendered with dynamic gesture and rich tonal contrast. Executed using the sugarlift (lift-ground) aquatint etching technique, the composition balances bold, painterly black brush-like marks with delicate textural reticulation and open tonal areas on warm cream paper. Designated as "Sugarlift" in pencil at the lower left margin, the work exemplifies early 1970s modernist studio printmaking with its playful character study and pronounced plate impression. Inscribed "Sugarlift" in pencil at lower left margin beneath the plate mark Signed and dated "S. Pearson 71" in pencil at lower right margin Distinct intaglio plate mark impression visible on both recto and verso Condition: Very good vintage condition. The paper ground displays mild, age-appropriate toning along the margins and minor edge handling wear consistent with age, while the ink impressions remain crisp and dark. Unframed, stored in a rigid clear protective sleeve.

rows.t: Large Framed Baby Portraiture Painting on Canvas Portrait Theme Single Piece

det.desc: Classical devotional imagery meets surreal distortion in this large original acrylic painting on canvas. A nursing child, encircled by a gold-toned halo, looks directly toward the viewer against a softly colored field of blush pink, ivory and pale yellow. Cascading, milk-like forms introduce a dreamlike quality, balancing maternal tenderness with an unsettling visual tension. The composition invites comparison with Madonna and Child imagery, particularly the tradition of the nursing Madonna. Read symbolically, the descending white forms suggest nourishment from a divine source, while the child’s unusually knowing gaze lends the figure a sense of spiritual awareness. These are interpretive possibilities rather than documented statements of the artist’s intent. Smoothly blended flesh tones and carefully modeled features contrast with the exaggerated drips surrounding them. That interplay allows a satirical reading: the painting adopts the visual authority of classical religious art while playfully disrupting its composure.
